trial_title: Efficacy of Dapsone as a Steroid Sparing Agent in Pemphigus Vulgaris
brief_summary: The purpose of this 12-month study was to determine the efficacy of dapsone as a glucocorticoid-sparing agent in maintenance phase pemphigus vulgaris.

eligibility_table.criterion: Histologic evidence compatible with pemphigus vulgaris and direct immunofluorescence evidence of pemphigus vulgaris.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has systemic mastocytosis, not pemphigus vulgaris, and there is no histologic evidence or direct immunofluorescence evidence for pemphigus vulgaris.

eligibility_table.criterion: Chronic disease that has been controlled with steroids and/or cytotoxics, e.g. maintenance phase.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's systemic mastocytosis is not described as being controlled with steroids or cytotoxics; rather, she is experiencing flares.

eligibility_table.criterion: On prednisone 15 or more mg/day to around 40 mg/day or on prednisone 15 or more mg every other day (qod) to around 40 mg qod.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is on a steroid taper, but the exact dosage of prednisone is not specified to be within the required range of 15 to 40 mg/day.

eligibility_table.criterion: Failure to taper steroids below a range of 15 mg/day to around 40 mg/day or 15 mg/qod to around 40 qod without flaring the disease.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has had flares and is currently tapering steroids, indicating she has not successfully maintained below the specified steroid dosage without flaring.

eligibility_table.criterion: The steroid dosage at which the most recent flare occurred should not be less than 85% of the last (within 30 days) dosage which controlled the disease, i.e. 85% of the baseline steroid dosage.
eligibility_table.justification: The information does not specify the steroid dosage at which the most recent flare occurred, making it unclear if it meets the 85% requirement.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a flare while on a steroid dosage of less than 85% of her baseline steroid dosage?

eligibility_table.criterion: Two baseline steroid dosages as determined by prior flares. It is common that patients will be repetitively unable to taper below a certain baseline steroid dose without experiencing a mild flare of their disease.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of steroid tapering, but specific baseline steroid dosages from prior flares are not provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a mild flare of pemphigus vulgaris when tapering below a baseline steroid dose of 125 mg IV steroids?

eligibility_table.criterion: No pulse steroids, pulse cyclosphosphamide, or plasmapheresis within two months of beginning the protocol.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication that the patient has received pulse steroids, pulse cyclophosphamide, or plasmapheresis within the last two months.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient understands the procedures and agrees to participate in the study program by giving written informed consent.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's understanding of the procedures and willingness to participate is not documented, making it unclear if she can provide informed consent.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient demonstrate an understanding of the study procedures as assessed by a standardized consent comprehension questionnaire with a score of ≥80%?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients able to taper steroids without recurrence of disease.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not been able to taper steroids without experiencing flares, indicating she does not meet this exclusion criterion.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients with early, severe disease that have not responded to high doses of prednisone, cytotoxics, plasmapheresis, or other modalities.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has systemic mastocytosis and has not responded to treatments, but the criteria specify early, severe disease, which does not apply here.

eligibility_table.criterion: Contraindications to the use of Dapsone, including severe anemia or G6PD deficiency.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient does not have documented severe anemia or G6PD deficiency, but this information is not explicitly provided in the profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a G6PD enzyme activity level below the normal threshold of 4.6 U/g Hb?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has behavioral problems that might interfere with compliance.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding behavioral problems that might interfere with compliance.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient been assessed for behavioral problems using a standardized questionnaire, such as the Child Behavior Checklist, with a score indicating significant concerns (e.g., T-score ≥65)?

eligibility_table.justification: The patient is a 22-year-old female, but there is no information regarding pregnancy or breast-feeding.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently pregnant or breastfeeding?

eligibility_table.criterion: Younger than 18 or older than 80 years of age.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is 22 years old, which does not meet the exclusion criterion of being younger than 18.
There is no documented history of allergy to dapsone in the patient profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient ever experienced an allergic reaction to dapsone, such as rash, itching, or difficulty breathing?

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of tachycardia but no documented ischemic heart disease.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented history of ischemic heart disease, defined as a previous myocardial infarction or coronary artery disease requiring intervention?
